name: Canadian Salad
description: Canadian Salad is a North American compendium trick-taking game where six hands are played in sequence with different objectives. In each hand, players try to avoid winning certain cards or tricks that bring penalty points. Also known as Wisconsin Scramble.
deck: 52 cards (with some cards removed for 3, 5, or 6 players)

history.origins: Canadian Salad is a North American compendium game, best known in Canada but also played under other names such as Wisconsin Scramble in other parts of North America. The compendium format (multiple hands with different objectives) is common in European games like Barbu and Herzeln.
timeline: Traditional origins: Developed in North America
Modern: Popular in Canada and parts of USA
Current: Many house rules and variants exist; players often add additional hands
history.cultural: Canadian Salad is popular as a social game and is often played with house rules. The compendium format makes it engaging as the objective changes every hand.
history.evolution: The basic six-hand format has been extended by many players who add additional hands with other objectives; house variants and extra hands are common.

setup.deck: 52-card standard deck. For 3 players: remove 2â™£ (17 cards each). For 5 players: remove 2â™£, 2â™¦ (10 cards each). For 6 players: remove 2â™£, 3â™£, 2â™¦, 3â™¦ (8 cards each). For 4 players: 13 cards each.
setup.dealing: All cards dealt evenly. Deal and play clockwise. First dealer chosen by cutting cards (highest deals). Turn to deal passes left after each hand.

rules.objective: Avoid winning cards and tricks that score penalty points. Six hands played in sequence with different objectives. Lowest total score after six hands wins.
rules.gameplay: Six hands played in fixed order: 1. No tricks - each trick = 10 pts (130 total). 2. No hearts - each heart = 10 pts (130 total). 3. No queens - each queen = 25 pts (100 total). 4. No king of spades - Kâ™  = 100 pts. 5. No last trick - last trick = 100 pts. 6. Combination - all above penalties apply (560 total). Player left of dealer leads. Must follow suit if possible; if cannot, may play any card. Highest card of led suit wins trick. No trumps. Winner leads to next trick.
keyRules: Hand 4: No king of spades (100 pts)

strategy.basic: Try to avoid winning tricks, especially in hands 1, 5, and 6. Get rid of high cards in dangerous suits early. In hand 4, avoid the king of spades at all costs.
strategy.intermediate: Count cards to track dangerous cards. In hand 2 (no hearts), try to become void in hearts early so you can discard them when other suits are led. In hand 6, the penalties stack dramatically - a single trick can cost hundreds of points.
strategy.advanced: Duck tricks by playing middle cards when possible. Force opponents to win dangerous tricks. In hand 6, calculate the maximum penalty a trick could cost. Long-term strategy across all six hands - sometimes taking a small penalty early prevents a larger one later.
tips: In Hand 2 (no hearts), try to get void in hearts early

Track which queens have been played in Hand 3
